name: Huddle
blurb: where churches and communities run events and get paid for them
tagline: where organisations bring their people together
summary: A modular event platform for churches, community groups, schools and NGOs in Nigeria and Ghana. Organisers create an event, attach Functions (Number Picker, RSVP & Seats, Extra Content) and share one link. Each Function can be free, paid through Paystack, or unlocked with an access code, and the money settles straight to the organisation’s bank.

cover.alt: Huddle landing page: Join the huddle. Connect, monetize your communities.

story: Huddle is for the people who run church services, community meetings and classes. They already meet on Zoom, Google Meet, Teams or in a room. Huddle runs alongside that meeting and adds the parts those tools lack: numbered turns, seats, recordings and notes behind a payment, and the payment itself.

An organiser creates an event, picks the Functions it needs from the Function Store, and shares one link, usually on WhatsApp. Attendees open it on their phones and join with just a name and an email. There are no passwords anywhere.
I built it end to end: the product, the event and dashboard flows, the database, payments and the tests. The first organisation is already running its events on it.

chapters.title: Functions, mixed per event
chapters.text: Every event is assembled from Functions. RSVP & Seats handles capacity, Number Picker lets attendees claim their own number, and Extra Content keeps recordings, notes and slides behind a gate. Each Function is gated on its own: free, paid, or unlocked with an access code.

images.alt: Huddle landing page: the Features section listing Number Picker, Vault, Voting & Polls, Q&A Queue, Certificate and RSVP & Seats

chapters.title: One link, no passwords
chapters.text: The event page is the whole attendee experience. It shows when and where the meeting is, a button to join it, and every Function attached to it. Attendees give a name and email once and are signed in with a magic link, so they never stop to create an account.

images.alt: Huddle public event page for In God’s Presence by The Watcher’s Voice, with date, place and a Join the meeting online button

chapters.title: Numbers, held and called live
chapters.text: Tapping a free number holds it for ten minutes while the attendee pays. A database constraint makes sure two people can never claim the same number, and the loser gets a friendly "someone just grabbed it". During the event the host calls numbers from one screen, and every attendee’s phone shows who is up within seconds.

images.alt: Huddle event page on a phone
Huddle Number Picker grid on a phone, numbers 1 to 30 at ₦100 each

chapters.title: Money goes straight to the organisation
chapters.text: Each organisation connects its bank once and gets its own Paystack subaccount. At checkout Paystack splits the payment: the organisation gets its share directly and Huddle’s 5% fee is taken automatically, so Huddle never holds anyone’s money. Payment confirmation is idempotent, so a late or repeated webhook can never grant something twice.

images.alt: Huddle event page showing a ₦100 Number Picker and a free Extra Content card with Prophesy Recordings

chapters.title: Tested against a real database
chapters.text: Gating, payments, holds, seat limits and anonymous pickers are covered by integration tests that run against a throwaway Neon Postgres branch, and Playwright walks the full organiser-to-attendee flow end to end.
